1.what: Hierarchical model (partially pooled effects for target, condition, sponsor, drug, area) against the registration baseline

2.what: Registration plus the precedent flag, for three link versions (today's; targets dated to June 2020; drug names and targets dated). Headline: the strict flag (experimental arms only) on the fully dated version

3.what: HOW (registration without therapeutic area), WHAT (disease, target, precedent, genetics, biology), and both
3.expectation: both beats HOW by +0.015 to +0.03; WHAT alone about 0.66

4.what: Phase 2 success by third of the WHAT score
4.expectation: top third beats bottom third by 15 to 25 per 100 trials

5.what: Split study with the test set as the "later" holdout, against random holdouts of the same size
5.expectation: a random split flatters the baseline by about 0.03 AUROC and hides the over-prediction

6.what: Per-trial predictions saved for the baseline and the models above
6.expectation: none; needed to draw development and test curves side by side

7.what: Intervals for the earlier results regenerated with resampling by lead drug

8.what: A biology-only score, within phase: (a) a count of six risk flags fixed in advance (target expressed in nearly every tissue; high expression in vital organs; gene essential to cells; intracellular target; drug activates its target; low drug-likeness), trials with two or more flags against trials with none; (b) a logistic model on biology columns only, top third against bottom third. No phase, sponsor, disease area, design, precedent, genetics or earlier outcome goes in. Thresholds are the ones fixed on trials before 2015; the logistic model is refitted on all development trials by the declared recipe
8.expectation: (a) 2 to 10 fewer successes per 100 with two or more flags; (b) 5 to 15 more in the top third. On development trials from 2015 to 2020 these were 8.1 fewer (14.6 to 1.7) and 16.6 more (10 to 23), and I expect them to shrink again. On trials whose targets appear in no development trial: same direction, too few to say more
